newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SHARES MIXED AT PRAGUE BOURSE DAILY FIXING.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SHARES MIXED AT PRAGUE BOURSE DAILY FIXING.

text.p: Czech shares were mixed at the daily price fixing on the Prague Stock Exchange on Friday, with most blue chips holding steady as investors wait out the current political storm.
Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna were the only continuously traded shares to rise as the Reuters RPIX index eased 2.5 points to 1,039.5 while the broader PX50 index edged up 0.6 points to 498.2.
Dealers said they expected little movement in prices in the coming days ahead of a confidence vote on the government of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus next week.
"Investors are just holding right now. After the vote we may see some renewed activity, but not before," said one trader at a foreign brokerage in Prague.
Confectioner Cokoladovny , majority owned by a consortium of Swiss Nestle SA and France's Danone, continued its upward path, rising 145 crowns to 4,050.

Dealers said the issue has gained favour with investors in recent days after the firm announced it would propose paying a 70 crown gross dividend per share on 1996 earnings, after 50 crowns in the previous year.
Cokoladovny posted net profit of 735 million crowns in 1996, after 516 million in 1995.
The firm holds its annual general meeting on June 31, dividends will be paid to shareholders registered on June 23.
The Swiss-French consortium Cokoladovny Partners hold an 81 percent stake in the Czech company.
